# ADR-066 — Checkpoint 9.7: personal intelligence is READ-ONLY, request-scoped, body-free by default, and cited ("Ask about today")

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Checkpoint 9.7 — Personal intelligence is READ-ONLY, request-scoped, body-free by default, and cited: "Ask about today" (2026-09-15, owner-approved D1–D5).** **No migration; level stays 20; no new table, column, role or index; no sixth `generateText` call site; worker untouched.** **D1 — model strategy: A.** The existing provider layer only, primary model only, through the existing `ask` task route (which already lets the owner pick any model on any configured connection). No local-model preparation, no hybrid. **D2 — first surface: B, "Ask about today".** Cloud Ask (8.6B) is widened with a bounded `TodayContext` and three one-tap preset questions; nothing else changes product shape — no Brief v2, no insight cards, no dedicated screen. **D3 — storage: A, never.** Answers exist only in the client's in-memory mutation result (TanStack mutation cache, no persister); no `job.output` class exists because the lane is synchronous. **D4 — proactivity: A, user-initiated only.** No cron, no push, no background generation; a preset chip is still an explicit tap, and a deep link with `preset=` only pre-fills — a test proves mount never calls the API. **D5 — limits:** `TodayContext` ≤ 12 000 chars (Brief parity; the Brief's own measurement shows the three time-critical sections alone reach ~8.6k on a busy day), `<records>` ≤ 5 000 chars / ≤ 4 records when Today is present (else the 8.6B 12 000 / 8), concatenated USER prompt ≤ 18 000 chars asserted before the call on the exact string sent (the static system prompt is excluded; worst case 12 000 + 5 000 + 512 + 238 framing = 17 750 — the review's arithmetic, which is why the records budget is 5 000 and not 6 000), 800 output tokens, answer ≤ 4 000 chars after the shared filter, exactly one model call per explicit request, `maxRetries: 0`, no client retry, single-flight. **1. THE CONTEXT CONTRACT.** `TodayContextSchema` (`packages/schema/src/intelligence-tools.ts`) is a closed, `.strict()` allowlist in the `BriefInput` tradition (ADR-043): overdue 8 · due-today 10 · upcoming 12 (≤ 3/day, 7 days) · events-today 8 · reminders 10 (7-day horizon, one-offs bounded to it for this caller only) · recently completed 10 (7 days) · projects touched 5 · unfiled captures 5 (160 chars, `redactSecrets` then truncate) · stalled projects 5 · projects without a next action 5 · snoozed-within-horizon 5 · review statuses. Both project lists carry an honest `total` beside their items, like every other section. **Every item carries an ordinal `ref`, never a uuid**; the `{type, id}` map lives server-side and is zipped into `sources` after the call (the 8.6B mechanism). **Every time is a server-formatted wall-clock string in the request `tz`** (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm`); UTC instants never enter the prompt, so the model never converts zones (the Brief still asks it to — recorded, not changed). Bodies, `rrule`, descriptions, `projects.goal`, `reviews.summary`, `event_external_links`, health, mail, monitor, OAuth, credential and AI-config data are excluded by construction; a key-set test pins the allowlist. The builder, `buildTodayContext(ReadContext)` in `apps/api/src/intelligence/`, reads ONLY through existing read models (`buildTodayResponse`, `collectRecentlyCompleted`, the reminders logic extracted from its route into `read-models/reminders.ts`) with ONE `effectiveNow`, requires the request-scoped Cloud Ask grant before any read, and applies a preset-aware drop ladder (the section a preset targets is never emptied; a dropped section keeps its honest `total`) — but the 12 000-char ceiling is a CONTRACT and the preset only a preference, so when JSON escaping of quote-heavy titles still leaves it over, protected sections are trimmed too. The build reports `lastRef`, the highest ordinal ever assigned, because the ladder leaves gaps in the surviving refs. `TodayEventItem` gained an OPTIONAL `origin` (ADR-064) so only external calendar text is passed to the output filter as provenance; unknown is treated as external. **2. THE TRANSMISSION CONTRACT.** `POST /ask { question, tz?, scope? }` — both new fields optional and additive. **Without `tz` the response is byte-shape-identical to 8.6B** (task/note sources only, refs from 1, no new fields), which is what keeps the versionCode 18 client's `.strict()` schemas parsing; a route test pins it. With `tz`: `scope: "today"` (what every preset sends) selects NO note or task body — `extractAskTerms`/`selectAskContext` are not called, proven by a counting `db` shim — because a chip about the schedule must never ship a journal entry that happens to contain "focus"; `scope: "both"` (free text) runs the 8.6B lexical selection beside the Today block with `refOffset` = the HIGHEST Today ref (`lastRef`), never the surviving citation count, which after a ladder drop would collide with a kept Today ref; the route additionally refuses to transmit at all if the Today and record refs are not disjoint. `scope` WITHOUT `tz` is `400 validation_failed` (it would otherwise select exactly the bodies the flag asks to exclude). **Citations are validated, not trusted:** every bracket group in the answer is parsed (lists and ranges expanded; the filter's own `[link removed]`, and any group with no digit at all, ignored; a numeric-shaped but malformed group — `[0]`, `[3-1]`, `[1.5]`, `[1,]`, an unsafe integer — counts as unresolved rather than vanishing) and an unresolvable ref is `502 ask_uncited` — a hallucinated citation is a failure, never a formatting quirk. An answer with NO citations is not refused (an empty day cites nothing) but returns `citations_present: false` and the client says so. **Ranking claims are NOT machine-verified — stated, not hidden:** the mitigation is the prompt ("overdue means listed in the overdue section; never recompute overdue, priority or slipping from times") plus server-authored `section` and `detail` labels on every source row (`[1] Overdue · P1 · title`) so a claim can be checked without opening the item (`[1] Overdue · P1 · title`; the detail never repeats the section word the client already renders). An empty day is answered locally by the client from the cached Today response with no cloud call. **3. THE CONSENT CONTRACT.** The `ask` route row remains the switch, but its disclosure now names every class that leaves (question; up to 4 matching bodies, secrets redacted by pattern only; titles/times/project names of tasks, reminders and events for today and 7 days, with calendar text marked as written by whoever created the invitation; 7 days of completions; the text of up to 5 unfiled captures; project names and counts; review status; nothing stored; provider handling unverifiable). Because the row is create-or-delete only precisely so a re-consent moment exists, **a row created before `ASK_TODAY_CONSENT_FROM` (the 9.7 release instant) is refused `409 ask_consent_outdated` on any `tz` request**; the client routes to Settings, where disable-then-enable re-consents under the new text. Production held no `ask` row at release, so no live consent was widened silently; the mechanism exists for every other database. ADR-061 D1's "note and task bodies … lexically preselected" is no longer the whole scope of the `ask` route — present-state pointer recorded here in the ADR-057 convention. **4. THE FUTURE-AGENT CONTRACT (designed, not integrated).** `READ_TOOL_NAMES` (`search_personal_items`, `get_item_context`, `get_today_context`, `get_calendar_context`, `get_task_context`), their `.strict()` input/output schemas and per-request budgets (≤ 6 calls, ≤ 30 000 chars, search limit ≤ 10/type, calendar span ≤ 14 days) are DEFINED in `packages/schema`; **exactly one implementation ships** — `buildTodayContext` is written so `get_today_context` binds it unchanged. No tool runtime, no binding, no loop, no `READ_TOOL_IMPLS`, no `posops_readonly` role (created only with the agent ADR; `ReadContext.db` is the same `Db` type regardless of role so the swap is zero call-site changes). A future `get_item_context` MUST assert the grant, redact and honour a bodies-consented flag — the ungated body read a wrapper-without-caller would rot into is why none ships now. **Guard 4** in `ai-egress-guard.test.ts` forbids any `ai`/`ai-providers`/worker import and any write verb under `apps/api/src/intelligence/`, and pins every tool name to `/^(search|get)_/`. **Ride-along:** Brief inbox snippets now pass `redactSecrets` before truncation (they were the one capture-derived string reaching a prompt unredacted). **Explicitly out and unchanged:** ADR-018, ADR-024, ADR-046 (health passive), ADR-052/054 (mail never in this context), ADR-056 (no embeddings, no pgvector, no write-capable lane), ADR-058, ADR-065; D1e; `ai_daily_briefs` retention (owner number, own item); the shared AI-call helper extraction (three `isAbortLikeError` copies remain). **Recorded, not fixed:** citation validation proves refs exist, not that claims are true; `redactSecrets` is prefix-shape only; `snoozed_within_horizon` sees only the 7-day window; the Brief still sends instants; `ASK_TODAY_CONSENT_FROM` is a code constant, not a stored disclosure version (Checkpoint 9.7, 2026-09-15)
